FWIW, some technical details to inform the wording: 
- Backup architecture: incremental snapshots written to object storage with lifecycle policies. We keep a 90-day rolling window in hot/cool tiers; older snapshots move to cold archive where deletion is governed by object lifecycle plus archive vendor retention.
- Purge mechanics: when a deletion request is processed we mark the customer ID deleted and start the purge pipeline. For hot/cool objects we can delete immediately where lifecycle allows. For cold/archive objects, deletion is queued and executed when archive vendor permits (usually within 30–120 days depending on vendor and region). That makes physical deletion "eventual."
- KMS/keys: we can destroy customer encryption keys on request, but destruction is disallowed if keys are needed for legal holds or active investigation. Key destruction is irreversible; we recommend documenting a 30-day cool-off before key destruction after a deletion request to allow for administrative reversal.
- Logs: audit logs are append-only for integrity; purging older audit records requires reindex/rewrite and has a ~48–72h job latency once triggered.

I'll annotate the retention_matrix.xlsx with the exact job timelines and vendor constraints — that should be sufficient for Laura to draft the consumer-facing text.

Jordan / FinCo team — thank you for the patience. Below is the consolidated playbook language and operational commitments we recommend you include in the DPA addendum. We are happy to tighten windows where we can, or include the addendum in your Master Service Agreement.

Summary of operational commitments (suggested DPA addendum language):
1) Primary store deletion: Redwood will logically remove customer-identifying pointers to deleted data within 24 hours of a verified deletion request.
2) Backup/snapshot purge: For Hosted customers, Redwood will make deleted customer data eligible for removal from backups and snapshots and will purge such data within a default 90-day rolling window. Due to snapshot immutability and subprocessors' archive constraints, physical removal from cold archive may be eventual (typically within 30–120 days of eligibility).
3) Dedicated/Reserved customers: retention window is configurable by customer (30–365 days); Redwood will honor explicit customer retention settings in their contract.
4) Private/on-prem: retention and purge are under customer control; Redwood will provide tooling and runbooks but does not have unilateral access to destroy private-hosted copies.
5) Logs and audit trails: security/audit logs default to 12 months retention, telemetry to 90 days. Customers may request shorter retention; security/legal holds can pause purge jobs and will be documented with start/end timestamps. Purge jobs for audit logs have an expected execution latency of 48–72 hours once triggered.
6) Subprocessors: Redwood will require subprocessors to adhere to DPA obligations and reasonable instructions to purge customer data. Where subprocessors' technical limitations delay physical deletion, Redwood will document the vendor and expected additional delay.
7) KMS / key destruction: Customers may request KMS key destruction; Redwood recommends a 30-day administrative cool-off after a key deletion request and a documented confirmation step. Key destruction is irreversible and may prevent future recovery.
